description.narrative: The CEACR, in its Observation on C87 adopted in 2019 (2020) (published in 2021), noted with satisfaction the following modifications introduced in the BLA: addition of section 182(7) instructing the Government to adopt SOPs for the processing of applications for registration of trade unions; repeal of section 184(2)–(4) imposing excessive restrictions on organizing in civil aviation; repeal of section 190(d) allowing cancellation of a trade union due to violation of any of the basic provisions of its constitution; repeal of section 202(22) providing for automatic cancellation of a union if, in an election for determination of collective bargaining agent, it obtains less than 10 per cent of the total votes cast; addition of section 205(12) stating that there is no requirement to form a participation committee in an establishment where there is a trade union; and addition of section 348(A) which provides for the establishment of a Tripartite Consultative Council to provide advice to the Government on matters related to law, policy and labour issues. The ILO played an active role to support in the amendment process of Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 in 2018 as well as adoption of EPZ Labour Act, 2019 to comply the CEACR observations with particular attention to consider the observations on C87. The ILO has also provided support to establishing a RMG sectoral Tripartite Consultative Council (RMG-TCC) as well as to the development of two Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) on trade union registrations and Unfair Labour Practices. Both the SOPs are integrated in the 2018 amended BLA, 2006.

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) has established in 2021 a tripartite monitoring Committee on the implementation of national roadmap of labour sector The Committee will meet at least once in 2 months. The first meeting is scheduled on 5 September 2021.
The Ministry of Labour and Employment has also established the Tripartite Labour Law Review Committee in order to discuss the amendment of labour laws so as to bring them into conformity with international labour standards. The committee is expected to meet at least once by the end of 2021. With the support of the European Union, the ILO had provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) for legislative reform in accordance with international labour standards.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) has submitted all article 22 reports due in 2021 by the deadline, except the report on MLC, 2006, which will be submitted in a few days. The ILO rigorously followed up on the timely submission of the reports. With the support of European Union, the ILO provided technical assistance to updating the report on C 81 following the concerns raised by CEACR in its report.
